Attention Is All You Need

A. Author
Abstract

The dominant sequence transduction models are based on recurrent networks. We propose the Transformer.

1 Introduction

Recurrent models [1] have cost OO(n^{2}) per layer.

Sequence models have long relied on recurrence and convolution to relate positions in a sentence. Recurrent computation is inherently sequential, which limits parallelism within a training example and becomes a bottleneck for longer sequences, because memory constraints limit batching across examples. We argue that attention alone can model these dependencies and describe an architecture, the Transformer, that dispenses with recurrence and relies entirely on attention to draw global dependencies between input and output.

2 Related Work

Earlier systems used gated recurrent networks and convolutional networks for transduction. Convolutional approaches relate signals from two positions with a cost that grows with the distance between them, which makes distant dependencies harder to learn than they are with attention.

5 Results

6 Conclusion

We presented the Transformer, the first sequence transduction model based entirely on attention. On the translation tasks reported above it can be trained significantly faster than architectures based on recurrent or convolutional layers, and it reached a new state of the art on the English-to-German task.
